title: Deepest ocean trenches
measure: Depth of each trench's deepest known point, in metres below sea level. Wherever possible the figure is a modern one: a multibeam sonar survey or a depth measured by a crewed submersible at the bottom. Many lists still repeat older single soundings from the 1950s, some of them out by up to 1,000 m.

entries.name: Mariana Trench
entries.note: The deepest point on Earth, 10,924 ± 15 m by multibeam sonar. Older figures of 11,034 m came from 1957 soundings.
entries.source: Bongiovanni, Stewart and Jamieson, Geoscience Data Journal (2021): multibeam sonar from the Five Deeps Expedition

entries.name: Tonga Trench
entries.note: 10,816 ± 16 m: confirmed as the second deepest point in the ocean.
entries.source: Bongiovanni, Stewart and Jamieson, Geoscience Data Journal (2021): multibeam sonar from the Five Deeps Expedition

entries.name: Philippine Trench
entries.note: Reached by the first crewed dive in 2021. Older lists give 10,540 m, from a 1951 sounding.
entries.source: Guinness World Records, Most deep-sea trenches visited by an individual: depths measured by the submersible Limiting Factor

entries.name: Kermadec Trench
entries.note: 10,003 ± 4 m, measured by calibrated instruments on the first crewed dive in 2021. Older lists give 10,047 m.
entries.source: EYOS Expeditions and Caladan Oceanic: depth measured by the submersible Limiting Factor

entries.name: Izu–Ogasawara Trench
entries.note: Depth reached by a crewed dive in 2022. The deepest point may be about 50 m deeper. Older lists give 9,780 m.
entries.source: Divernet, First humans dive Japan's ocean deeps (2022)

entries.name: Kuril–Kamchatka Trench
entries.note: A 2020 multibeam survey found it about 1,000 m shallower than the 10,542 m many lists still give.
entries.source: Dreutter et al., Progress in Oceanography (2020)

entries.name: Santa Cruz Trench
entries.note: Reached by the first crewed dive in 2021.
entries.source: EYOS Expeditions and Caladan Oceanic: depth measured by the submersible Limiting Factor

entries.name: New Britain Trench
entries.note: The deepest point on Earth with no documented descent, crewed or robotic.
entries.source: Gallo et al. (2015), via Wikipedia, New Britain Trench; WorldAtlas

entries.name: Yap Trench
entries.note: 8,929 ± 9 m, reached by the first crewed dive in 2020.
entries.source: EYOS Expeditions and Caladan Oceanic: depth measured by the submersible Limiting Factor

entries.name: San Cristóbal Trench
entries.note: Reached by the first crewed dive in 2021. The Puerto Rico Trench, the deepest in the Atlantic at 8,378 m, is next.
entries.source: EYOS Expeditions and Caladan Oceanic: depth measured by the submersible Limiting Factor
